# Field-work desk

The field desk continues from an approved municipal dispatch. Supervisors plan visits and assign named crews; crews record field outcomes, notes, files, labor, materials and equipment; supervisors review the saved work and prepare destination update packages.

## Open the workspace

Use Node 22.16 or later with the complete installed product source.

```sh
node cli.mjs init --workspace /absolute/path/to/field-work
node cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/path/to/field-work --port 8770
```

Open the loopback URL printed by the server. The header identifies the current directory, workspace and revision. **Save workspace** downloads the complete editable handover.

## Import approved work

In **Approved source work**, choose the original dispatch JSON or a complete editable follow-through workspace. Give this source a name and use **Inspect source**. If the original workspace contains several dispatches, select the intended saved dispatch ID from the inspection, then import it.

The original JSON is retained in full. A visit refers to one row in that saved dispatch, including the original request, confirmed related orders, approved work, source geometry and mapped delivery values. The source list is searchable and paginated; it does not truncate the imported programme.

Use **Plan visit** beside the intended request. The location view plots valid WGS84 points from the current source page. Records without usable WGS84 points remain available in the table.

## Plan crews and visits

In **Crews**, save the crew name, available members, roles and contact details. Mark a crew available for assignment as appropriate.

A visit has a title, approved source row, optional crew, priority, instructions, planned start/end and due time. The field record is separate: field outcome, actual start/end, completion or exception note, field notes, resource entries and files.

Date entry uses the browser's displayed time zone. Saved date/time values identify UTC instants. Opening and saving an unchanged time preserves the original instant, including its original seconds.

Each field note has its own stable ID, author, recorded time and text. Each resource entry has a stable ID, type, name, explicit unit, exact decimal quantity, optional unit cost and currency. Decimal values allow at most 18 whole digits and 9 fractional digits. A cost requires a three-letter currency. Quantities and costs are kept by their declared unit and currency.

**Add files** retains the complete bytes in the workspace. Save the visit to include the selected file IDs in its field record. Removing a file from a visit changes that visit's references while the original saved file remains in the workspace history.

Each save creates a new visit version. The interface checks the current version before saving an open edit. If a saved browser draft belongs to an earlier version, the current version opens with a download for the earlier draft so the operator can compare the work.

## Work offline with a crew package

Select one or more visits in the visit register and choose **Create crew package**. Selection can span pages. Name the package and provide its operating instructions, then save it.

Download **Offline crew editor** and provide that complete HTML file to the crew. It opens directly in a current browser, without a field-desk server or a network connection. The package includes the selected visit versions, source records, assigned crew details and existing field file bytes.

The crew can move between visits, change the field outcome, enter actual times and completion notes, add field notes, record resources, and attach files. The editor saves its draft and file bytes in browser storage where available. The storage namespace includes the original package ID and hash. The editor reports if browser storage cannot retain a change; downloading the return preserves it in a file.

Enter a return name and the person or crew returning the work, then choose **Download crew return**. The resulting JSON includes the original package identity, each changed visit's original version, and only the changed field keys. A returned note/resource list represents that changed field in full; its stable item IDs allow the supervisor to reconcile overlapping entries. Omitted visits and fields are unchanged.

Original municipal report media remain part of the original source record. New files entered with a visit are separately recorded in the field record. The original source links can be opened explicitly when a connection is available.

## Review crew returns

In **Returned work**, import the complete returned JSON. Open it to compare each proposal against the visit sent to the crew and the current workspace version.

For each pending proposal, choose **Leave for later**, **Accept reviewed changes**, or **Reject these changes**. An accepted proposal with an overlapping field requires an explicit choice between the current and returned values. Changed source context and changed assignments have their own review acknowledgements. The interface shows the actual compared values, rather than inferring that a completed crew status changed the municipal request.

Enter the supervisor's name and review note, then save the selected decisions. Partial decisions leave the remaining proposals pending. Acceptance creates the resulting visit version and binds its supervisor approval to the exact source context and version. A later field edit or relevant source change makes that approval require a new review.

An operator can also review a saved visit directly from its detail page or select several visits and choose **Review selected visits**. The review opens the saved field record and original source work for each selected current version.

## Prepare destination updates

Select reviewed visits and choose **Prepare destination update**. Name the package, identify the reviewer and destination, and choose the destination action for each visit.

**Update field information** carries the reviewed field work. **Request destination closure** additionally requires completed field work and current supervisor approval. Destination references and item notes identify the intended customer records.

The saved package binds the destination, original source records, approved visit versions, supervisor decisions, resource quantities/costs and included files. Download its JSON, CSV, GeoJSON or report for the destination workflow. The field outcome, supervisor approval and requested destination action remain distinct values throughout.

## Save and continue a handover

**Save complete editable workspace** includes all source records and original text, crew and visit versions, attachments, saved crew packages, original returns, supervisor decisions, destination packages, and retained operations.

To continue a separate handover, initialize an empty field desk directory, open **Open a handover**, and receive the complete editable JSON. The new directory adopts the original workspace identity and history. Continue editing, assigning visits, reviewing returns and creating updates in that received workspace.

## Recover an interrupted operation

The browser retains a mutation's request ID, original body, expected revision and workspace identity before sending it. If the response is interrupted, **Recover the saved operation** remains visible.

Use **Check completion** to read the retained operation by its original request ID. **Resume saved operation** resends that same original request when no completed operation is found. A completed request returns its saved result. The pending-operation namespace follows the workspace directory, so recovery also works when receiving a handover changes the workspace UUID.

Form drafts are kept separately from submitted operations. Recovered visit or supervisor-review drafts are applied only to the version and source comparison from which they were made. Earlier drafts can be downloaded when the current work has changed.

## Access and presentation

The server listens on its exact loopback host and port. It checks the request origin and the current workspace identity for mutations. The browser assets are local; the interface and portable crew editor do not depend on a CDN.

The workspace uses a neutral industrial layout, keyboard-accessible forms, labelled tables and dialogs, responsive sections, and a print layout. Complete record details, original files and editable handovers remain available from the same operating views.

# Install municipal field work and crew returns

The **open311-field-desk** source selection delivers the complete municipal product: service collections, service reporting, GIS handoff, request/work-order Follow-through, and Field Desk. Each application opens its own saved private directory. Complete original exports connect the desks.

## Build the selected source

From the maintained repository checkout:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo . --ref EXACT_ACCEPTED_SOURCE_COMMIT \
  --selection open311-field-desk \
  --out /absolute/new/field-desk-package --offline
~~~

Choose the accepted source commit and a new output directory. The selection preserves the existing merchant, releases, runtime installer, Applications and file-reader components. Its additive contribution registers the Field Desk command, browser assets, typed exports and merchant provider.

Direct Field Desk modules need Node.js 22.13 or newer with built-in SQLite. The complete installed merchant runtime requires Node.js 22.16 or newer, Linux, Python 3.11 or newer and util-linux flock. The installed source remains under package/source.

| Installed export | Interface |
| --- | --- |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/seller/open311-field-desk | Original dispatch, crew, visit, return, supervisor and destination APIs and types |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/seller/open311-field-desk/workspace | Durable editable SQLite workspace |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/open311-field-desk | Native merchant provider and initializer |
| @tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/open311-field-desk/client | Typed adapter for an existing merchant callTool transport |

## Prepare the original private runtime

Run from the directory where the delivered merchant package is installed. Use its actual archive and complete SHA-256:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install prepare \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime \
  --archive /absolute/handover/ORIGINAL_MERCHANT_ARCHIVE.tgz \
  --sha256 ORIGINAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature schema --feature openapi --feature mcp --operator

npx --no-install starforge runtime-install install \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime

npx --no-install starforge runtime-install inspect \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime --load --source
~~~

The prepared runtime uses its delivered package/source and selected node_modules. Continue an interrupted installation with runtime-install resume --dir and the original directory. A populated cache supports --offline --cache /absolute/private/npm-cache. Offline native preparation also needs the compiler and Node headers for the selected executable; --node-headers names the prefix containing include/node.

## Initialize or receive the desk

Initialize a new saved desk:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311-field-desk init --workspace /absolute/private/field-desk
~~~

A full delivered Field Desk workspace is received into an empty destination:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311-field-desk receive \
  --workspace /absolute/private/received-field-desk \
  --input /absolute/handover/editable-field-workspace.json \
  --request-id receive-field-desk-001 --expected-revision 0
~~~

Receiving preserves original dispatches, crews, visits, attachment bodies, issued packages, returned proposals, supervisor decisions, destination packages and original operation history. The saved database is open311-field-desk.sqlite. Select the received directory when opening its application.

## Open Applications

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  open311-field-desk serve \
  --workspace /absolute/private/field-desk --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0
~~~

The single LISTENING record identifies the loopback URL, workspace UUID, saved-directory binding and live server instance. Open the URL to establish the browser session.

In merchant Applications select **Open311 field work and crew returns**, then the same initialized or received directory. Its source-owned provider reads the original database identity, binds the launch arguments to that directory and verifies the actual live startup response. Receiving into an open empty desk follows the imported workspace identity while retaining directory-based browser recovery.

## Bring selected approved work into the field

Export either the complete reviewed dispatch JSON or full Follow-through workspace from the earlier application. Field Desk source inspection lists actual dispatches when a workspace has several. Select one original dispatch and give its retained source a useful name.

Use the browser to save the named crew, create visits from selected dispatch rows, and issue the chosen visits as crew JSON or complete self-contained HTML. The crew editor opens locally, preserves drafts and produces a partial return carrying its original package and visit versions. The supervisor imports that return, reviews conflicts and explicitly approves destination updates.

[MCP.md](MCP.md) supplies private host configuration, the full typed client and original-file receiving. [WORKSPACE.md](WORKSPACE.md) covers the complete supervisor and crew interfaces. [README.md](README.md) gives direct CLI and source usage.

## Deliver an editable customer workspace

Deliver the complete Field Desk workspace JSON with the chosen crew and destination files, the operating guide and accepted installed source identity. Original attachments travel inside the complete packages. The receiving operator can reopen the issued visits, inspect original returned files, continue partial decisions and create later destination packages.

# Municipal Field Desk

Field Desk takes a reviewed municipal Follow-through dispatch through named crew visits, complete files and resource entries, partial field returns, supervisor decisions and destination update packages. The browser, CLI and typed merchant provider share the same saved SQLite workspace.

Start with [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) for the complete installed merchant product or [WORKSPACE.md](WORKSPACE.md) for the operator interface. [MCP.md](MCP.md) describes the complete installed automation workflow.

## Original source and operating identity

Import either a complete commons.open311.follow-through-dispatch.v1 JSON file or a complete commons.open311.follow-through-workspace.v1 file. The latter retains all original request/order files and operating history. Select its actual dispatch ID when it contains more than one dispatch.

Each imported row keeps its original request, selected orders, reviewed relationship, approved work, destination columns and exact source hashes. Field Desk accepts unchanged approved work carried forward into a later Follow-through edition while preserving the work's original approval edition.

A visit has its own identity and immutable versions. Its source binding records the dispatch, request, order and approval editions. Several visits can belong to one original request. Subsequent source imports expose changed or missing source rows beside the original visit context.

Original request status and closure notes remain source data. Visit field status is planned, assigned, in_progress, completed, unable or cancelled. Supervisor approval is recorded separately against the selected visit version. A destination package names update or request_closure explicitly for each selected visit.

## Direct local commands

From this source directory with Node.js 22.13 or newer:

~~~sh
node cli.mjs init --workspace /absolute/private/field-desk
node cli.mjs inspect-source \
  --input /absolute/handover/follow-through-workspace.json

node cli.mjs import \
  --workspace /absolute/private/field-desk \
  --input /absolute/handover/follow-through-workspace.json \
  --dispatch ORIGINAL_DISPATCH_ID --name "Reviewed municipal work" \
  --request-id field-source-001 --expected-revision 0

node cli.mjs serve --workspace /absolute/private/field-desk --port 8770
~~~

Every mutation takes a stable --request-id and the observed --expected-revision. Read status before preparing a new command. A dropped response is recovered by operation --request-id and an exact repeat of the original command. A later revised selection receives a new request ID.

| Command | Input and result |
| --- | --- |
| crew-save | Named crew, members, contact details, notes and active state |
| visit-save | Source ID/key, crew, schedule, priority, instructions and field record |
| attach | Complete original --file and declared --content-type |
| package | Name, explicit visitIds and optional note |
| return-import | Complete original field-return JSON |
| decide | returnId, reviewer and selected proposal decisions |
| review | Reviewer and exact visit-version approve/return_to_crew selections |
| update | Named destination and selected current approved visit versions |
| receive | Complete editable Field Desk workspace into an empty destination |

crew-save and visit-save accept either the bare record or its named wrapper. Other command files use the corresponding fields documented in index.d.mts. Action files may include the request ID and revision; explicit CLI arguments choose those same control values.

## Crew work and resource records

A crew stores its name, named members, each member's optional role/contact, note and active state. A visit chooses that crew, source row, priority, planned start/end, due time, instructions and field record. Scheduling and actual timestamps retain explicit offsets; missing times remain null.

Field notes carry an ID, author, text and recordedAt. Resource entries carry ID, kind, name, exact decimal quantity, unit, optional unitCost/currency and note. Decimal values are strings with up to eighteen integer and nine fractional digits. For example, quantity "1.25" and unit "hours" preserve the entered precision. A missing rate stays null; an entered rate has its explicit three-letter currency.

Resource totals combine matching kinds, names and units, with monetary totals kept by currency. Original historical work-order costs remain available inside source context. Field Desk retains original attachment bytes and hashes, and reuses identical bytes while keeping declared aliases.

## Issue and receive crew work

Create a package from the explicit current visit IDs. Export kind crew-html for the complete offline editor or crew-json for its complete data. The HTML includes the issued visit baselines and selected attachment bodies. It saves local drafts, accepts original field files, and exports only selected changed visits as a field return.

A return identifies its original package and baseline visit versions. Import retains the complete original return before supervisor decisions. Review displays original, returned and current field values. Each proposal can be accepted or rejected; overlapping values offer returned/current choices. Assignment or source changes remain visible and require the applicable explicit acknowledgement. Omitted proposals remain pending.

A later edit produces a new visit version. Supervisor review applies to an exact version, so a destination update selects the version whose current approval matches. Exported update packages retain field observations, resources, source rows, original relationship decisions and selected attachments.

## Complete exports

~~~sh
node cli.mjs export --workspace /absolute/private/field-desk \
  --kind crew-html --package ISSUED_PACKAGE_ID \
  --out /absolute/handover/crew-work.html

node cli.mjs export --workspace /absolute/private/field-desk \
  --kind update-report --update SAVED_UPDATE_ID \
  --out /absolute/handover/reviewed-destination-report.html

node cli.mjs export --workspace /absolute/private/field-desk \
  --kind workspace --out /absolute/handover/editable-field-workspace.json
~~~

| Kind | Selection and complete file |
| --- | --- |
| workspace | Entire editable workspace and original files/history |
| source | sourceId; unchanged original approved dispatch or Follow-through workspace |
| crew-json / crew-html | packageId; full issued data or offline editor |
| returned | returnId; unchanged original field return |
| visits-csv | Optional source/crew/status/search filters; complete matching register |
| update-json | updateId; full source-linked destination package and files |
| update-csv | updateId; operational rows, exact resource totals and identities |
| update-geojson | updateId; source-bound locations and null geometry for unlocated rows |
| update-report | updateId; printable selected work, decisions, resources and source context |

The CLI creates private output files without replacing an existing file. Merchant exports use the maintained retained reader and can stream full bytes. The unchanged full-workspace export uses its saved timestamp, preserving its identity across reader release and process reopen.

## Source API

~~~js
import { openWorkspace } from './workspace.mjs';

const desk = openWorkspace('/absolute/private/field-desk', { create: false });
try {
  const state = desk.state();
  const first = desk.visits({ limit: 100 });
  const file = desk.exportFile({ kind: 'workspace', expectedRevision: state.revision });
  // Persist file.body as complete bytes; file.sha256 and file.bytes identify that export.
} finally {
  desk.close();
}
~~~

The public declarations in index.d.mts cover every source, crew, visit, return, decision, destination and receiving object. The HTTP server exposes the same operation model to the browser. The installed provider and client add host-selected original files, revision-aware paging and complete retained downloads.

[SOURCE_CONTRACT.md](SOURCE_CONTRACT.md) and [SOURCE_REGISTER.json](SOURCE_REGISTER.json) preserve the supplier source interpretation and original Follow-through format references.

# Field Desk merchant tools and typed client

The **open311-field-desk-workspaces** provider operates the same saved Field Desk as the browser and CLI. Its normalized configuration key and family are **open311FieldDeskWorkspaces**. The maintained host configuration field is **open311FieldDeskWorkspaceConnection**.

Prepare the complete selected merchant product using [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). Initialize each saved operating and receiving directory before selecting it in the host configuration.

## Host-selected original files

Save a private connection JSON file with mode 0600. [examples/host-connection.json](examples/host-connection.json) contains the complete shape. Its schema is stellar-forge.open311-field-desk-host.v1.

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.open311-field-desk-host.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "operations": {
      "label": "Municipal field work",
      "directory": "/absolute/private/field-desk",
      "inputs": {
        "dispatch": {
          "label": "Complete reviewed municipal dispatch",
          "path": "/absolute/handover/reviewed-dispatch.json",
          "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_COMPLETE_ORIGINAL_FILE_SHA256",
          "kind": "source",
          "format": "json"
        },
        "returned": {
          "label": "Original crew return",
          "path": "/absolute/handover/crew-return.json",
          "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_COMPLETE_ORIGINAL_FILE_SHA256",
          "kind": "return",
          "format": "json"
        },
        "context": {
          "label": "Original selected task context",
          "path": "/absolute/handover/task-context.json",
          "sha256": "REPLACE_WITH_COMPLETE_ORIGINAL_FILE_SHA256",
          "kind": "attachment",
          "format": "binary",
          "contentType": "application/json"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
~~~

Replace every hash placeholder with the full SHA-256 of the actual complete file. Relative paths resolve from the connection file. Workspace aliases select distinct original private directories; file aliases select exact original files. Each configuration supports up to 128 workspaces and each workspace up to 128 original input aliases.

| Input kind | Format | Complete input |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source | json | Approved Follow-through dispatch or editable Follow-through workspace |
| return | json | Original partial or complete crew return |
| workspace | json | Editable Field Desk workspace |
| attachment | binary | Original file bytes with the declared media type |

A JSON attachment uses attachment/binary to preserve its original bytes as a visit file. JSON source, return and workspace inputs are decoded strictly as UTF-8. The configured file SHA and the action's expectedSha256 must match the actual entire file before import.

readFieldDeskWorkspaceConfiguration(path) validates the configuration and original directories. FIELD_DESK_HOST_SCHEMA exports the exact schema. readFieldDeskHostInput(entry, alias, expectedSha256) returns the selected complete bytes and metadata.

Each file mutation records the original alias, kind, format, complete SHA and declared media type alongside the original action. File selection is part of request replay, including when two aliases happen to refer to identical bytes.

## Initialize the maintained merchant host

Save setup options:

~~~json
{
  "directory": "/absolute/private/field-desk-merchant",
  "connection": "/absolute/private/field-desk-host.json",
  "name": "Municipal field work"
}
~~~

Use the original prepared runtime:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  merchant-providers init open311-field-desk-workspaces \
  --options /absolute/private/field-desk-setup.json
~~~

The equivalent source function is initializeFieldDeskMerchantWorkspace from mcp-setup.mjs. An optional releaseStore selects an existing original SF82 release store. Otherwise the maintained initializer prepares one. The setup keeps its original input and saved attempts, so the same arguments resume an interrupted setup.

Generate the merchant client entry on the host that will launch it:

~~~sh
npx --no-install starforge runtime-install run \
  --dir /absolute/private/municipal-runtime -- \
  merchant-mcp-client-config \
  --config /absolute/private/field-desk-merchant/merchant-mcp.json \
  --name open311-field-desk \
  --output /absolute/private/field-desk-mcp-client.json
~~~

The generated entry uses that host's actual Node and prepared stdio source paths. The maintained --merge option preserves an existing client configuration while adding an unused server name to a new output. The direct transport is merchant-mcp-stdio --config through the same runtime.

## Complete operating catalog

Names begin with merchant_open311_field_desk_.

| Suffix | Customer operation |
| --- | --- |
| workspaces / status | Original aliases, current identity, revision, counts and saved operation summaries |
| records | Page sources, crews, issued packages, returns or destination updates |
| input / inspect_source | Verify the original host file and inspect its actual dispatch choices |
| import_source / source / source_rows | Save full original context, inspect its definition and page complete source rows |
| crew_save / crew | Save named crew versions and read membership history |
| visit_save / visits / visit | Save, search and inspect visits, source changes, files and history |
| attachment_save | Retain complete original file bytes and their declared media type |
| package_create / package | Issue selected current visits and inspect the complete package by pages |
| return_import / return | Retain original crew return and inspect proposals, conflicts and decisions |
| decisions_apply | Accept/reject selected exact proposals with explicit overlap choices |
| visits_review | Approve selected current visit versions or return work to the crew |
| update_create / update | Save and inspect selected approved destination updates or closure requests |
| operation | Recover an original request result and its input identity |
| receive | Reopen the whole editable history in an empty selected desk |
| file_read / file_release | Deliver or release complete retained files |

Reads of saved records require expectedRevision. They return workspaceId/revision with items, total, offset, limit, returned and nextOffset. Merchant pages accept 1–100 items; follow nextOffset until null. Large original row bodies and complete packages remain available through file delivery.

source returns dispatch definition, totals and a row count; source_rows carries the original rows. crew pages history. visit pages history or attachment metadata while returning the current visit, source row, crew and approval. package pages visits or attachment metadata; update pages selected items or attachment metadata. return pages proposals or saved decisions. Select section explicitly when changing those views.

All mutations require requestId and expectedRevision. Read status to prepare a new action. Recover a dropped response using operation with the same request ID; if it has no saved result, retry the original complete input. Validation and revision failures roll back. Changed selections use a new request ID.

## Typed operating example

The client adapts an existing merchant transport:

~~~js
import { Open311FieldDeskMerchantClient } from
  '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/open311-field-desk/client';
import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';

const desk = new Open311FieldDeskMerchantClient(
  (name, args) => merchantTransport.callTool({ name, arguments: args }),
  'operations',
);

let state = await desk.status();
const source = await desk.importSource({
  input: 'dispatch',
  expectedSha256: originalDispatchFileSha256,
  name: 'Reviewed municipal work',
  requestId: 'field-source-001',
  expectedRevision: state.revision,
});

const crew = await desk.saveCrew({
  requestId: 'field-crew-001',
  expectedRevision: source.revision,
  crew: { name: selectedCrewName, members: selectedCrewMembers, active: true },
});

const rows = await desk.sourceRows({
  sourceId: source.source.id,
  expectedRevision: crew.revision,
  offset: 0,
  limit: 100,
});

const visit = await desk.saveVisit({
  requestId: 'field-visit-001',
  expectedRevision: crew.revision,
  visit: {
    sourceId: source.source.id,
    sourceKey: selectedOriginalSourceKey,
    crewId: crew.crew.id,
    title: selectedVisitTitle,
    instructions: selectedInstructions,
    priority: 'normal',
  },
});

const issued = await desk.createPackage({
  requestId: 'field-package-001',
  expectedRevision: visit.revision,
  name: selectedPackageName,
  visitIds: [visit.visit.id],
});

const delivered = await desk.downloadFile({
  kind: 'crew-html',
  packageId: issued.package.id,
  expectedRevision: issued.revision,
});
await writeFile('/absolute/handover/crew-work.html', delivered.bytes, {
  flag: 'wx',
  mode: 0o600,
});
~~~

Select the actual original source key from the paged source rows. Creating additional visits continues from the last saved revision. Named crew/member values and visit instructions belong to that operating desk.

The offline crew editor exports a complete original field-return file. Configure it as a new return input alias and retain its actual whole hash. Then call importReturn with input, expectedSha256, requestId and expectedRevision. Inspect returned with the saved return ID and section proposals.

applyDecisions takes returnId, reviewer and selected decisions. Every decision names proposalId, accept/reject and expectedVisitVersionId. Conflicting changes use fieldChoices with changeId and returned/current. Source or assignment changes require the applicable acknowledgement. Unselected proposals remain pending.

reviewVisits selects exact visit versions for approve or return_to_crew. createUpdate selects the current approved versions and names the destination, reviewer and update/request_closure action. The full input interfaces are declared in index.d.mts and mcp-client.d.mts.

## Full byte delivery and receiving

downloadFile(selection, options) returns {file, bytesRead, bytes}. bytes is a Buffer. Options include chunk limit, maximumBytes and async onChunk; a streaming sink receives complete bytes without the accumulated Buffer.

Every chunk keeps its original file name/type/size/hash, byte offset and selected workspace revision. The client checks exact base64, counts, continuation progress, terminal length and whole SHA-256. Original retained snapshots remain stable across later browser changes. A failed download exposes the original selection, expected hash and offset for reconciliation.

| File kind | Required item |
| --- | --- |
| workspace | Complete desk; no item selector |
| source | sourceId |
| crew-json / crew-html | packageId |
| returned | returnId |
| visits-csv | Optional sourceId, crewId, status and q |
| update-json / update-csv / update-geojson / update-report | updateId |
| attachment | attachmentId; complete original bytes |
| operation | operationId; complete retained original input and result |

All file selections require expectedRevision. A saved operation view replaces large source/return/attachment bodies with their original byte/hash descriptors. Its complete body is available as an operation file. A workspace-receive operation keeps a compact original-file descriptor and incoming package hash to preserve repeated handovers without recursive copies of whole prior packages.

To receive an editable desk, configure its actual complete JSON as a workspace input in an initialized empty destination alias. Call receive with that alias, expectedSha256, a new stable request ID and expectedRevision 0. The receiver validates and reconstructs original sources, crew and visit versions, attachment bytes, issues, field returns, partial decisions, approvals and destination packages.

## Ownership and normal shutdown

The provider lazily opens its own existing database handles. Closing it waits for admitted operations, closes its retained readers and releases those handles. An independently running browser continues with the same saved workspace. Applications, release initialization, private host inputs and complete file delivery use the maintained merchant contracts.

# Municipal Field Desk: source and operating contract

This contract describes the implemented Field Desk under `open311/field-desk/`. It connects an approved municipal request/work-order dispatch to crew planning, field returns, supervisor decisions and an editable receiving workspace. The complete original dispatch remains attached to each field action.

Implementation basis: the complete twelve-file core in [source capsule 5c89942e12571e28995e0c6633e413bc95abc4fc](https://api.github.com/repos/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/git/blobs/5c89942e12571e28995e0c6633e413bc95abc4fc), 126,098 UTF-8 bytes, SHA-256 `6f68e432c38e275af87babf9e071920bb515c2c9e43aaa007384c211af3700c6`. The complete typed interface is `index.d.mts`, Git blob `05779d33797c2ba84484a367bb12abb27721ced0`. Source intake uses `source.mjs` at `8ff71aeb982a979eaedb4377381e772077faed2c`; durable receiving uses `workspace.mjs` at `24e0b9a58f36d8faf4bc033fddb7dd2779b2a20b`.

## 1. Customer workflow and primary sources

The following published workflows motivate the product. Their product descriptions establish operating needs; the corresponding Field Desk behavior is the implementation described in the remaining sections.

| Primary source | Published operating need | Implemented Field Desk behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Connected Bits: Spot Workers, integration layer and partners](https://connectedbits.com/) | Assign field tasks, record status, photographs and completion notes, supervise queues and connect CRM, GIS, assets and work orders. | Versioned crews and visits; a portable crew editor; exact attachment files; returned field changes; supervisor review; source-linked destination packages. |
| [Catalis Request311](https://catalisgov.com/public-works/request311/) | Reassign, update and close requests while retaining history and integration context. | Field visits retain the approved request/order source binding, original history and local action history through export and receiving. |
| [Catalis: Public Works Efficiency with Citizen Request Management](https://catalisgov.com/request311/public-works-efficiency-with-citizen-request-management/) | Mobile crews need request information and equipment/material context during field work. | Issued packages contain selected visits, their original source rows, crew details and files. Returns include exact labor, material, equipment and other resource entries. |
| [Catalis: Inventory Tracking & Work Order Management](https://catalisgov.com/inventory-tracking-work-order-management/) | Schedule and assign maintenance work with resource and mapped-asset context. | Crew assignment, planned and actual times, due time, priority, instructions, resource quantities and costs, with original mapped source context. |
| [Catalis GIS WebMap](https://catalisgov.com/public-works/geographic-information-system/) | Field work depends on municipal asset and geographic information. | Original effective source geometry travels with the approved dispatch and destination export. The implemented field form edits the field record defined below. |

These are primary sources read for this implementation on 12 October 2026. The citizen-request management article is dated 12 November 2025. `SOURCE_REGISTER.json` preserves the original source URLs, observed sections and the source pins for the preceding Follow-through product.

The proposed adoption work is to configure this operating handoff for an agency's supported systems and actual source files. An implementation profile must identify the agency, service groups, crews, destination system, source meaning and acceptance workflow.

## 2. Original dispatch intake

The importer accepts either complete sealed `commons.open311.follow-through-dispatch.v1` JSON or a complete sealed `commons.open311.follow-through-workspace.v1` JSON export. A workspace may contain several dispatches. `inspectSource` reports all available dispatches and whether a selection is required; `importSource` records the selected dispatch ID with the complete original input text.

A saved `commons.open311.field-source.v1` retains the complete original file, its UTF-8 byte count and SHA-256, the selected original dispatch, source series, edition ID and seal, and any originating workspace UUID and revision. Source rows preserve:

- The complete normalized request, its original values and source SHA-256.
- The complete explicitly approved associated orders, each with its own identity and source SHA-256.
- The saved approved local work and its original approval context.
- The original effective geometry and destination-column mapping.
- The dispatch definition, coverage and totals.

The intake validates the original seals and selected source versions. Approved work carried forward from an earlier edition remains valid when its original request and order versions still match the selected dispatch. This preserves an existing approval across an unchanged source edition.

Request identity, order identity, approved work identity and field visit identity are distinct. An approved row can contain zero associated orders. A missing or unavailable published order source remains part of the original source context.

A visit's `SourceBinding` includes source ID/hash, series, dispatch ID/hash, edition ID/hash, source key, request ID/hash, approved work ID/hash, every linked order key/ID/hash and the complete selected row hash. The original source status remains available as source data throughout field work.

## 3. Crews, visits and time

A crew is a versioned roster with `name`, `members`, `note` and `active`. A member has `id`, `name`, `role` and `contact`. Saving a crew records its prior version. New assignments select an active crew; an existing assignment can retain its historical inactive crew.

A visit selects one imported source row and an optional crew. Its planning fields are `title`, `plannedStart`, `plannedEnd`, `dueAt`, `priority` and `instructions`. Priority is exactly `low`, `normal`, `high` or `urgent`. Saved visits retain crew identity/version/name, source binding, prior visit version, creation time and the cause of the saved change.

Planning and actual time inputs require an explicit time-zone offset. An end time cannot precede its corresponding start. Original source date-only values remain in the original source object; an agency chooses any additional interpretation in its source configuration.

The editable field record has the following exact vocabulary:

| Field | Accepted content |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | `planned`, `assigned`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `unable`, `cancelled` |
| `actualStart`, `actualEnd` | Offset-bearing timestamp or null |
| `completionNote` | Text |
| `notes` | Entries with stable `id`, `author`, `text`, `recordedAt` |
| `resources` | Entries described in section 4 |
| `attachmentIds` | IDs of retained exact attachment files |

The current crew/visit model uses this roster, assignment and field-record vocabulary. Geographic context comes from the original approved source row. Visit filtering supports source, crew, local field status and text, with paginated results.

Saving a visit creates a new version. A visit can explicitly select a successor dispatch for the same original series, source key and request identity. Its history then records the new source binding.

## 4. Exact resource entries and attachments

Each resource entry has stable `id`, `kind`, `name`, `quantity`, `unit`, optional `unitCost`, optional `currency`, and `note`. Kind is exactly `labor`, `material`, `equipment` or `other`.

Quantity and any unit cost are nonnegative decimal strings with at most 18 whole digits and 9 fractional digits. Examples are `"2"`, `"0.75"` and `"18.500"`. The implementation calculates sums and products using exact integer/scale arithmetic. A unit cost requires an uppercase three-letter currency code. Quantities are grouped by kind, name and unit; money totals remain grouped by currency. Original source work-order costs remain in their source records alongside these newly entered field resources.

`putAttachment` accepts filename, content type and complete base64 file content. Stored identity is based on the SHA-256 of the decoded bytes. Byte count, content hash, exact bytes and original descriptors are retained. Reusing identical bytes preserves additional filename/content-type descriptors as aliases. A visit refers to stored files by attachment ID.

An original request photograph can be imported as source-context material, with its original URL and request identity recorded in the accompanying source or note. Its evidential meaning follows its actual origin. A crew note and returned file describe a field observation only when that is what their original content records.

The complete issued and receiving packages carry referenced files. Binary input through the merchant host records its original alias, hash and content type before entering the same attachment operation.

## 5. Issuing a portable crew package

`createPackage` freezes a named, nonempty selection of saved visits. A `commons.open311.field-crew-package.v1` contains:

- Package ID, producer workspace UUID and revision, creation time, name and note.
- Each exact visit baseline, its source summary and complete original dispatch row.
- The selected crew details and all referenced attachment content.
- The package SHA-256 seal.

Export `crew-json` carries the full structured package. Export `crew-html` carries the portable editor for that package. Both preserve the same package ID, seal and original visit version IDs.

The crew receives the original request/order context, assignment and field inputs together. A later return identifies the package it used, so the supervisor can compare the actual issued baseline with subsequent office edits.

## 6. Receiving field work and reconciling changes

The complete return input has schema `commons.open311.field-return.v1`, original `packageId` and `packageSha256`, name, returned-by identity, optional note, a visit array and optional complete new attachments.

Each included visit names `visitId`, its issued `baseVersionId` and a partial `fields` object from the exact field-record vocabulary in section 3. A return can cover part of the issued package. Omitted visits and omitted field keys remain unchanged. An included list field supplies the intended list against its package baseline; stable entry IDs allow additions, edits and deletions to be compared individually.

`importReturn` retains the complete original text, original-file byte/hash identity, package reference, supplied attachments and generated proposals. The original package baseline, current saved visit and returned values remain available together.

The comparison works at the following granularity:

| Field type | Comparison |
| --- | --- |
| Status, actual times, completion note | Original, current and returned scalar value |
| Notes and resources | Stable entry ID, including additions and deletions |
| Attachments | Membership of each attachment ID |

A conflicting change means that the current value differs from both the issued baseline and returned value. Each conflict requires an explicit `current` or `returned` choice. Source-context and assignment changes are shown separately from field-value conflicts.

A supervisor applies decisions using the pending proposal ID and expected current visit version. Each proposal is accepted or rejected, with reviewer and note. Accepted work with changed source or assignment context requires the corresponding explicit acknowledgment. A decision records its full selected changes, choices, original baseline, observed current version and result.

Accepting a return creates a new visit version when its field data changes and records supervisor approval of the resulting exact visit/source context. Rejecting a proposal retains the current visit and its recorded rejection. Partial decisions leave the remaining proposals pending.

## 7. Supervisor approval and destination actions

`reviewVisits` supports `approve` and `return_to_crew` for explicitly selected current visit versions. A direct approval with changed source context requires the visit to select its intended current source; the return-decision path also supports an explicit source-change acknowledgment. Every approval is tied to the exact visit version and source context it reviewed.

`createUpdate` selects current approved visits, names a destination `name` and `system`, and optionally records the destination's reference. Per-visit actions are exactly `update` and `request_closure`. A closure request additionally requires local field status `completed`.

The sealed `commons.open311.field-destination-update.v1` contains each full visit, original source row, source binding, original dispatch definition, crew, supervisor approval and referenced files, together with resource totals and action counts. It carries both the intended local destination action and the original external source values.

This operation produces a reviewed destination handoff. The external municipal request/work-order system remains the authority for its own recorded state. Installation work configures how the agency receives this package through its supported integration or operator process.

Exports are complete JSON, CSV, GeoJSON and an HTML report. CSV uses the maintained reversible spreadsheet-formula escaping. Geographic exports use the original effective source geometry. Unlocated and exceptional source values remain available in the complete JSON/source records.

## 8. Durable workspace and independent receiving

The SQLite workspace saves complete source records, every crew and visit version, attachment bytes and aliases, issued packages, complete returns, decisions, supervisor reviews, destination updates and successful operation history.

Each write requires a caller's stable `requestId` and observed `expectedRevision`. Reusing a request ID returns its original result only when the operation and input identity match. A conflicting revision or different action under the same request ID produces a conflict.

The complete export has schema `commons.open311.field-desk-workspace.v1`. It includes producer UUID/revision, original creation and update times, records, full operation inputs/results, receiving history and its seal. An unchanged workspace uses its saved update time for deterministic export identity. The complete portable package limit is 256 MiB.

Independent receiving opens a new empty Field Desk workspace at revision zero. `receive` validates the complete original package and replays its operation history to check records and results. It then imports the original history, preserves the producer workspace UUID and records a new receiving operation and receipt. The receipt includes the destination's original UUID, origin UUID/revision, complete original-file byte/hash identity and package seal. The received workspace advances to the original revision plus one and remains editable.

A receiving request ID must be distinct from the imported operation history. An exact repeat of that receiving request returns its saved result. Subsequent work continues with the received workspace's observed revision.

## 9. Interfaces and complete exports

The shared core exposes source inspection/import, crew and visit management, attachment import, package creation, return import, decisions, supervisor review, destination updates, complete export and receiving. Read operations provide state, individual original operations, full objects and paginated source rows/visits.

The HTTP and CLI interfaces use the same workspace operations. The typed merchant integration uses the original file transport for JSON source, return and workspace inputs, and binary attachment inputs. A retained host input descriptor identifies alias, original SHA-256, kind, format and optional content type. Revision-aware reads and writes let the installed application continue the same saved operation.

| Export kind | Complete intended content |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace` | Editable workspace and full original history |
| `source` | Exact imported source text |
| `crew-json`, `crew-html` | Issued package or its portable editor |
| `returned` | Exact imported return text |
| `visits-csv` | Selected visit rows |
| `update-json` | Complete approved destination package |
| `update-csv`, `update-geojson`, `update-report` | Destination table, geographic view and readable report |

## 10. Agency implementation and original-source interpretation

A deployment agrees its source fields, service groups, crew roster, dates, resource units/currencies, destination references and supervisor responsibilities. The source profile records the actual provider's ID, date, status and coordinate semantics.

For the existing municipal source editions, request and order identifiers remain distinct. Manatee's request-only edition retains its actual work-order retrieval errors and original geometry/declared CRS. Omaha's original request and order records retain their explicit relationship decisions, literal source date strings and source-generated object-ID behavior. Public request attachments retain their actual report origin. These are configuration and source-context facts for the agency handoff.

The acceptance journey follows the product's complete operating path: import the original approved dispatch, assign saved visits, issue a portable package, receive partial field work, decide actual changes, approve selected current visits, prepare a destination update, export the editable workspace, receive it into a new workspace and continue from its recorded revision.

Actual source captures, operating outputs and implementation profiles establish the particular deployment's result. This contract defines the implemented data and action semantics that those deployments use.
